headline: MinerU’s MCP-enabled document pipeline creates the main pairwise risk; LightZero is isolated and mostly lowers interaction severity.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no file, network, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot be directly hijacked. MinerU can ingest documents and expose an MCP server, so if its outputs are manually bridged into LightZero prompts, prompt injection becomes possible, but only through unusual operator-mediated copy/paste or file handoff.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into LightZero prompts or a shared MCP channel is introduced, injection becomes plausible.
IF LightZero remains isolated from external text inputs, this pathway stays blocked.
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the two agents.
Copy only sanitized summaries, not raw MinerU output, into LightZero.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text.
Review MinerU outputs for instruction-like content before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between document extraction and downstream prompting.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no filesystem or network and lists no data classes, while MinerU processes local documents and OCR text with allowlisted egress. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling evidence, so leakage is limited to operator-chosen document transfer rather than a default cross-agent spill.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is fed to MinerU and then exported into LightZero-visible logs or prompts, leakage occurs.
IF MinerU is configured to send extracted content to an external API, exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of shared folders.
Run MinerU on a separate workspace from LightZero.
Turn off any export-to-chat or export-to-LLM step.
Redact OCR text before passing it onward.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, and MinerU also cannot write files or modify git. With no overlapping write authority to the same mutable resource shown in either profile, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict could emerge.
IF future tooling adds shared mutable state, reassess this verdict.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared assets.
Avoid mounting a common writable workspace.
Do not grant git write permissions to either agent.
Use separate output directories per agent.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing system that can produce extracted text, tables, and OCR output, and LightZero is a game-playing agent with no verification or document-analysis role. If MinerU’s extracted content is forwarded into LightZero or another downstream consumer as authoritative, errors can cascade; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF MinerU output is treated as ground truth by a downstream agent, cascading errors can propagate.
IF LightZero is used to act on MinerU-extracted facts without verification, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted facts before reuse.
Compare MinerU output against the source document for critical fields.
Do not let LightZero act on unverified extraction results.
Use confidence thresholds for downstream consumption.
requires-engineering: add validation and provenance checks between extraction and action.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is evidenced in either profile. LightZero lists no data classes or secrets, and MinerU’s profile shows no handled secrets or regulated-data commitments, so a compliance breach pathway is not supported here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into MinerU, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF either agent is deployed under a stricter policy than shown here, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair unless policy is reviewed.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Confirm where MinerU stores extracted artifacts.
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated data.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
